title: Preface
summary: This OCR-garbled FBI file excerpt (Part 1 of 9, BUFILE 61-7099) on Albert Einstein covers his proposed inadmissibility to the United States under the Alien Exclusion and Deportation laws. It cites a State Department request that consuls deny him a visa, the burden-of-proof doctrine, and Supreme Court precedents on alien exclusion. It alleges Einstein advocated anarchist and communist causes, affiliated with the War Resisters International and related groups, and endorsed revolutionary and anarchist ideas, including a 1932 Lyon address and a fund he authorized. It also discusses anarchism's opposition to government and the State.

nodes.summary: The text is a garbled OCR scan of an essay critiquing Albert Einstein as a 'militant pacifist' and anarcho-communist. It argues that Einstein's writings, speeches, and affiliations (with Frau Rosika Schwimmer, the War Resisters International, and his 1950 'Militant Pacifism' address) promote shattering the state, military, and laws, and encourage draft resistance. It cites Einstein's 1930 letter to Heywood Broun, a 1931 New York Times article, and the Schwimmer Supreme Court case, and quotes Lenin and Marx on revolution and state destruction.

title: February 16. 1950
summary: A February 16, 1950 letter to Walter Winchell, apparently from or about Albert Einstein, OCR-garbled. It says Einstein has been a long-time listener of Winchell's radio broadcasts and lists many organizations Einstein belonged to or sponsored, such as the American Council of Soviet Friendship, Abraham Lincoln Brigade, Victims of German Fascism, and a petition to abolish the Dies Committee on Un-American Activities. nodes.summary: The text is a garbled OCR scan of a memorandum about atomic energy history. It states that Einstein received his formal education in Germany. Per the Smyth Report, Einstein in 1905 proposed that mass and energy are equivalent and suggested this might be proven by studying radioactive substances. In July 1939, Einstein wrote a letter to President Roosevelt, delivered via Alexander Sachs, a friend of Roosevelt. Roosevelt acted by granting $6,000 for research, which led to the uranium/atomic bomb program. Leo Szilard, a USN figure, is also mentioned.

nodes.summary: A 1950 FBI memorandum from H. B. Fletcher summarizes government files on Professor Albert Einstein. It covers his marriages, his 1933 emigration to the US and 1940 naturalization, and his 1939 letter prompting Roosevelt's atomic research funding. It also describes a 1946 Soviet invitation he declined, criticism of Soviet anti-Semitism, and a 1950 Atomic Energy Commission note that he never received formal clearance. The memo lists his affiliations with organizations cited as communist by the Attorney General and congressional committees, plus miscellaneous groups. It notes his peace activism, his Emergency Committee of Atomic Scientists work, and his anti-militarization and world-government views.
